title: Request Journey Explorer: timeline-first trace inspector and correlation drilldown
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Build a timeline-centric trace inspector inside Redwood Console that lets engineers inspect a single request’s journey end-to-end: spans, timeline, token-level events, correlation IDs, and lightweight cost attribution. This ticket captures the design prototype, review notes, trade-offs, and handoff artifacts for a tracing drilldown view optimized for LLM inference workloads.
user_stories: As an SRE, I want to paste a correlation ID and jump to the full request timeline so I can debug latency spikes quickly.
As an ML engineer, I want to see per-span token counts and estimated cost so I can identify expensive model calls.
As a product engineer, I want to compare traces between rollout variants to see cost/latency regressions after a model switch.
As an on-call engineer, I want a compact summary row (p50/p95/total-cost) and a link to raw request JSON and logs for fast incident response.
design_goals: Make trace data digestible with a timeline-first UI rather than a long flat span list.
Surface correlation IDs, request metadata, and model/route tags prominently.
Support quick filtering (route, model, region, customer id, trace id) and timeline zooming to inspect token-level events.
Keep the UI performant for traces with hundreds of spans via virtualization and lazy loading.
Provide actionable links: raw request JSON, linked logs/Grafana panel, GitHub PR (rollout) and ability to save a trace permalink.
proposals: Primary canvas: horizontal timeline with rows representing services/components (ingest, router, runtime, kernel, model). Spans drawn as bars with color by component and width = duration.
Left rail: summary card with trace id, route, model, total latency, token counts (input/added/output), estimated cost, and action buttons (Copy ID, Open logs, Open raw request, Save permalink).

Span panel: clicking a span expands a right-side detail pane showing span annotations, start/end times, parent/child links, host/pod, and a small flamechart for internal operations (batching, kv-cache hit/miss, quantization cost).
Correlation waterfall: collapsible view that groups spans by correlation_id prefix so related asynchronous work (background caching, fallback model calls) is visible inline.
Comparison mode: select two traces to overlay timelines or show synchronized timelines to compare latency and token distribution across rollout variants.
feedback: PM (Ava Morgan): prioritise copy-to-clipboard for correlation IDs and ensure per-trace permalink supports RBAC-aware access.
Engineering (Liam Chen): prefer server-side pagination for span lists and an API that can return span aggregates to avoid fetching entire traces by default.
Security (Priya Nambiar): verify that raw request JSON view redacts customer PII by default and respects data residency flags.
Design review: reduce visual noise by hiding low-duration spans under an aggregated marker; allow 'expand all' for deep debugging.
technical_considerations: Tracing API needs endpoints: GET /traces/{id}?expand=timeline, GET /traces?correlation_id=..., and GET /traces/{id}/compare/{id2}.
Backend should compute per-span estimated cost (token_count * model_unit_cost) and supply a pre-aggregated cost-per-span metric to avoid client-side heavy compute.
Frontend must virtualize span rows and implement canvas/WebGL rendering for large traces to keep 60fps when zooming.
Privacy: raw payloads must be gated behind permission checks and redact keys flagged by KMS/audit config.
acceptance_criteria: Search by correlation ID works from global console header and opens the trace inspector with the correct trace highlighted.
Timeline shows per-span duration, parent-child relationships, and span metadata (component, host, model tag).
Span detail pane shows token counts, estimated cost (USD), and links to raw request JSON and linked logs.
UI remains responsive with traces up to 500 spans (virtualization/lazy load verified in perf tests).
Permalink to trace preserves applied filters and respects RBAC (unauthorized users cannot open the raw request view).
next_steps: Design handoff: prepare final Figma spec with component states, responsive behavior, and tokens (due 2025-03-05).
Engineering kickoff: sync with runtime and backend teams to finalize trace API contract (meeting 2025-03-07).
Security review: submit payload-redaction checklist to Security for approval (owner: Priya Nambiar).
Prototype user testing: schedule 3 sessions with SRE and ML Eng to validate filters and cost-attribution UX (target: Cycle 2025-W11).
